name: Nile Blue
lede: Nile Blue is a pale, soft blue-green with a name taken from the river, recorded in color charts since the 1880s.

sections.title: A river's color
sections.body:
Paterson gives Nile blue as a greenish-blue and adds that the name is also a chemical blue stain used on fatty acids; Nile green, he says, is the pale green of the river Nile, also called *eau de nil* [1]. The swatch here is documented in Ridgway's color nomenclature (the 1886 edition and the plate of 1912), in the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 (block 163), and in the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930, which gives 1884 for its first recorded use [2]. Ridgway's plates are aged scans, so the swatch is approximate [2].

The ISCC-NBS name is "very light bluish green", 7.2 CIEDE2000 units away, and the nearest name in our learning set is powder blue, 8.7 away [2]. For related colors see [[aquamarine]], [[sea-green]] and [[turquoise]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 22 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive carry a color near it, 0.09%, as photographed [3]. In 46% of the 13 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays a light [3]. The earliest dated match is a painting by Mathieu Dubus of 1639, which comes 247 years before the name's earliest record in our sources, so it is a look-alike hue and not proof of a dye [3]. In printed English the phrase peaks in the 1940s [4].
